text:
aisha nguyen: FYI nightly eval flagged a regression after the promptset rebaseline we landed yesterday (rebase v9). negation F1 down ~6.4% on model-x-2q, mostly on 'never/except' cases. throwing this up for quick triage.

eval-bot: nightly-evals · model-x-2q · promptset/rebase-v9
- test_suite: pset-negation-v2
- baseline: 0.912 F1
- current: 0.856 F1
- delta: -0.056 (6.14%)
- failing cases: 342 / 5,621
(see /evals/2026-03-19/pset-negation-v2/model-x-2q)

samir patel: ugh. is this the rebase that removed the few 'edge' negative examples?

aisha nguyen: yeah looks like we removed the small targeted prompt that taught the model to anchor 'never' scope. the diff is small but concentrated.

mike lopez: can you paste the prompt diff? want to eyeball whether it's wording change or splitting examples.

aisha nguyen: here's the diff we applied (human-edited):
```
- Q: If the user says they never want notifications, should we send any alerts?
- A: No, never send alerts.
+ Q: User prefers no notifications. What is allowed?
+ A: Respect preferences and avoid sending unwanted alerts.
```

riah singh: that tweak looks like it softened the explicit 'never' -> could cause boundary shift. might be a calibration/regression rather than model change.

samir patel: quick experiment idea: run a tiny canary using v9 promptset but force the old targeted prompt back in for the negation subset. if that fixes it, rebaseline was the cause.

aisha nguyen: good call. I'll craft a canary patch to insert the exact old prompt for the negation partition and run the nightly eval subset.

eval-bot: scheduled job: canary-eval/negation-patch started (job id: ce-7832). will report in ~12m.

mike lopez: in parallel, can we surface examples that flipped? need small set for QA to confirm behavior.

aisha nguyen: pulling top 50 diffs now (worst confidence delta). attaching a sample: 
- Input: "I will never sign up for that feature. Do not remind me"
- Baseline: "No reminders."
- Current: "Consider subtle reminders."

riah singh: yikes. that's a clear semantics shift. happy to run manual evals on those 50.

eval-bot: canary-eval/negation-patch result: delta restored to -0.8% (within noise). regression reproduced and mitigated by adding the old explicit prompt back.

aisha nguyen: OK that confirms the prompt wording change caused the drift. options: 1) rollback rebase v8 for production and we iterate on a cleaner rebase. rollback reduces blast radius quickly., 2) patch rebase to re-add explicit negation prompt and re-run rebaseline (slower), 3) keep v9 and accept regression (not an option).

samir patel: my vote is rollback to v8 for production and we iterate on a cleaner rebase. rollback reduces blast radius quickly. :+1:

mike lopez: prefer targeted patch + canary if we can ship it within the hour. less churn for downstream teams. :thinking_face:

aisha nguyen: timebox: if we can green-canary in 45m I'll do patch; otherwise I'll roll back.

riah singh: QA can prioritize the 50 diffs for manual sign-off. ping me when canary result is in.

eval-bot: canary-eval/negation-patch final: pass (restored). runtime 00:09:12.

aisha nguyen: canary looks good. patch is minimal, reapplying explicit negative anchor. I'll open a PR to update rebase artifacts + add an automated check to flag softening of absolute keywords during rebase.

samir patel: please add a changelog note and notify platform teams. also mark rebaseline v9 as "hotfix-patched" so we don't auto-roll forward.

mike lopez: +1 to adding the automated check. less manual triage next time.

aisha nguyen: PR: https://git.internal/rebases/patch/4387 (adding prompt back, unit test for negation anchors). planning to merge after one more review and then redeploy rebaseline artifact. target: +30m.

riah singh: LGTM, will run the manual 50-case QA after merge.

aisha nguyen: thanks everyone. I'll post a short summary to #eng-ml after merge and update the rebaseline docs. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

samir patel: moving forward, can we add a small eval step in the rebaseline pipeline that checks for keyword polarity shifts for critical prompt families?

aisha nguyen: agreed — adding to the Rebaseline checklist.

mike lopez: thanks team. great fast loop.

eval-bot: incident-note: regression triage closed, mitigation deployed (patch v9.0.1), rollback not required.
